instruction: From the daily folder in Thunderbird, sorted by oldest to newest, select the first three emails and enter their sender name, subject, and date into a LibreOffice Calc file called 'first_three.xlsx' on the Desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting first 3 emails sorted by ascending date from daily folder. Verified by parsing all 9 emails: first 3 by date are Jan 21 (eNotices System), Jan 22 (HKU Bulk Email Delivery System), Jan 23 (eNotices System). Custom getter extracts first 3 rows with sender, subject, date; custom metric validates exact match with expected values. Partial matching on date allows flexibility in formatting.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Each email contributes 1/3 to total score. Within each email: sender_name (0.33), subject (0.34), date (0.33). Date matching allows partial string matching for format flexibility.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies file existence at /home/user/Desktop/first_three.xlsx
Getter properly extracts first 3 rows with sender_name, subject, and date columns from xlsx file
Metric correctly validates exact count (3 emails) and compares each field (sender_name, subject, date) against expected values
Expected values are semantically correct: first 3 emails by ascending date (Jan 21, 22, 23) verified from actual email data
Postconfig appropriately activates window and saves file to ensure fresh state
Partial credit scoring (1/3 per email, distributed across fields) is logical and fair
Minor issue: Header detection in getter (line 38-41) is fragile - only checks row[0] for keywords, but adequate for typical xlsx structure
Minor issue: Date matching logic uses very flexible substring matching which could theoretically cause false positives, but acceptable for format flexibility
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider strengthening header detection to check all columns, not just row[0]
Consider more precise date matching (e.g., normalize date formats before comparison) to avoid potential false positives from substring matching
